binary.reason: DecodeHiveBinaryFrame branches on BINARY: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. A compressed part of any other frame inflates to at most 32 MiB (wire.go), and one that would inflate further, or is truncated, is refused. ListenBinary delivers it. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself.

browser-login.reason: BrowserLogin and InteractiveLogin on ControlPlane (browser_login.go). BrowserLogin refuses a cleartext API URL before anything is asked (requireSecureTokenExchange, native_auth.go), reads GET /v1/auth/native/config (a 404 stays the API's *APIError with a display line saying browser sign-in is not offered; a 2xx that is not a usable object is an ErrAPI error with no status; ParseNativeSignInConfig applies the endpoint, client id and S256 rules), binds 127.0.0.1:0 (tcp4, SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE on Windows in loopback_windows.go) before building the URL (BrowserAuthorizationURL: the fixed parameter order, RFC 3986 encoding with a space as %20, scope left out when no non-empty scope is asked for, device_name cut to 120 code points), prints the URL or hands it to Prompt, opens it with the Opener on its own goroutine or the platform browser (openWith, control.go), and waits on the monotonic clock. loopback.go reads request heads itself rather than through net/http's server, as the reference reads them over asyncio streams: a 16 KiB cap, the request line as Latin-1, no Host required, nothing logged. classifyRequest serves GET /callback only (else 404); a missing, repeated or wrong state is a 400 and the wait goes on (subtle.ConstantTimeCompare); an error wins over a code; values are decoded as parse_qsl decodes them. The first right-state callback is accepted and the port closed; its tab is answered once the sign-in has ended, with the page headers on every answer; close waits at most 1 s for that tab, closes every other connection, and returns once every listener goroutine has. The exchange posts exactly code, code_verifier, client_id and redirect_uri to the configured token_endpoint, keeps the token through acceptToken (device_login.go) so RevokeAPIToken revokes it the same way, and takes the code, the verifier and the state out of every field of a refused exchange's *APIError. Denied and expired are the device-login types (errors.go) with a nil APIError; a callback without a code is *BrowserLoginFailedError (ErrAPI, with the page's error as Code), since Go's APIError cannot say no status. InteractiveLogin: auto signs in through the browser when CanOpenBrowser holds and the configuration is usable, and with a device login otherwise (loginWithDevice in control.go, given the Opener); browser and device force one; nothing falls back once the URL is shown. browser_login_vectors_test.go runs all 119 cases of browser-login-vectors.json and records each one: the pure sections against their functions (every callback case also through a real listener), and sign_ins and chooser for real over a loopback httptest API and a raw TCP browser, the chooser's machine set with t.Setenv and browserPlatform. browser_login_test.go covers the prints, the opener's goroutine, the listener's edges, goroutine accounting on every path and secrets in errors. The reference's final round (39e31d8, 119 cases): every control-plane request is refused off the API's origin (sendRequest in control.go, a no-status ErrAPI error); token_endpoint has no colon and only whole %XX escapes; authorization_endpoint is on port 1-65535 with a host, as written, that is a bracketed IPv6 address, an IPv4 address or ASCII hostname labels; a callback error keeps only RFC 6749's seven codes; only a nil DeviceName gets the default (an empty one is left out, and the device fallback sends no client_name); the accepted tab waits until the sign-in ends; a HEAD answer has headers and no body; the exchange answer is redacted before formatting in one pass, longest first, never wholly inside an existing [redacted] (a value spanning one is still matched whole); and every answered connection is drained (write side shut, at most 2 s / 1 MiB read) before it closes. Go's own additions, none changing a vector's outcome: the exchange goes through sendNoReplay (control.go) without GetBody, so the HTTP transport never sends it twice; any access_token, refresh_token or id_token in a refused answer is redacted; a ctx done by the time Prompt returns opens nothing; a []string method list is read; and the listener handles at most 64 connections at once; a refused answer over 1 MiB or carrying more than 64 distinct tokens is omitted rather than echoed, and the scrubber is built once per answer, without a regular expression; an oversized HEAD gets a 400 with no body.

device-login.reason: BeginDeviceLogin, PollDeviceLogin and RevokeAPIToken in device_login.go, one step each, for a caller that runs its own loop; LoginWithBrowser in control.go now runs its loop over the same one-poll path. A pending poll is a *DeviceLoginPendingError carrying Interval, and slow_down lengthens the DeviceAuthorization's Interval for good; expiry and denial are *DeviceLoginExpiredError and *DeviceLoginDeniedError (errors.go), still matching ErrDeviceCodeExpired and ErrDeviceAccessDenied, and every one of them reaches the *APIError the API answered with. Every sign-in (password, native in native_auth.go, browser, device poll) goes through acceptToken, which sets AccessToken and TokenID from its own answer. Revoking the token in use is idempotent: a 401 on its own revoke counts as revoked, and revoking again sends nothing until the next sign-in. DeviceAuthorization and APIToken print with the device code and the token redacted. Run against the shared device-login vectors over a loopback httptest server, checking every request, with what the SDK produced recorded. 0.9.1: DeviceLoginOptions.ClientID and BeginDeviceLoginWithOptions send a registered app's client_id (HomeAssistantClientID is thalovant-home-assistant) and leave it out when empty; BeginDeviceLogin keeps its signature. DescribeDeviceLogin reads GET /v1/auth/device/codes/{user_code} as the approver into a DeviceLoginRequest, whose ClientVerified is true only with a ClientID. A 2xx token answer that is not a JSON object is a plain ErrAPI with no status. APIError.GoString keeps %#v from printing Problem, which can echo the request. 0.15.0: LoginWithBrowser runs through loginWithDevice (control.go), which opens the verification page with InteractiveLogin's Opener when one is given (openWith: on its own goroutine) and with the platform browser exactly as before otherwise; the device-login vectors and the existing LoginWithBrowser tests pass unchanged.

home-link.reason: home.go: HomeRequest, HomeAnswer, HomeResponse, PlainSpeech and DecodeReferences (real tags only, via rich.go's StripSSML; numeric references, the XML five and  ; Unicode White_Space), AnswerHomeRequest and AnswerHomeRequests. The hub's 10 s run from arrival: the handler gets its 9 s or what is left, on its own goroutine, and the answer goes out at the deadline whatever the handler does; the reply gets what the handler left, is never started after the bound, and is withdrawn when it passes. A handler or a Replier that ignores its context keeps its goroutine until it returns, since Go cannot stop one; while four handlers are still running past their time a request is answered timeout at once without starting its handler, and while four replies are, no reply is started and the error says so (the reference runs at most four plain handlers at once). Each AnswerHomeRequests subscription keeps its own counts; AnswerHomeRequest on its own shares one count of handlers and counts replies per Replier (an uncomparable Replier value is not counted). client.go: Client.Reply and ReplyContext, built from the context as the hub sent it; a destination with no source gets no destination. session.go: HubSession.On, OnStateChange, Reply, Connect and Run, and LinkSupervisor, the pure decision Run follows after every attempt (drop: at once; failure: the ladder; refusal: the ladder through a 600 s grace; changed key: stop). transport_wss.go: closeRefuses, the pure close rule (1000/1005/1008 during the handshake or within 750 ms after it, a code up to 250 ms late), a handshake answer that does not authenticate is a refusal, a 401/403 upgrade is a refusal, and a failed KK is followed at once by one XX in the same connect -- as it is over HTTP (transport.go) and MQTT (transport_mqtt.go), through the shared noiseChannel in transport_noise.go, which reads a failed handshake as a refusal the same way. noise_store.go: a pin mismatch is ErrHubKeyChanged, never a refusal. Run against the shared home-link vectors and link-keeping vectors: the close and supervise cases through the pure functions, the handshake cases over real WSS Noise against a loopback hub that records the patterns it saw. 0.9.1: a close after a frame that decrypted under the session's keys -- any frame, a chunk and the hub's encrypted HELLO included -- is a drop (closeRefuses' afterAuthenticatedFrame). A refusal right as an XX handshake ends, with nothing from the hub in between, is a *ClientKeyRejectedError (errors.go: ErrClientKeyRejected wraps ErrHubRefused), naming the key folder and the other likely one (noise_folder.go); after KK the same close is a plain refusal; LinkSupervisor gives up at once on LinkClientKeyRejected. Over HTTPS a 401/403 while or right after the last XX frames go out is the same verdict, and HTTPTransport.ClosedRefused reports the HTTP refusal. A reply's wait for the send path is withdrawable; a frame already being written is finished whole (errFinishing), on every transport, and the link is kept. The queued cases run over a real WSS link.

Docs say that delivered means the hub handed the speech to the speaker's connection (no playback receipt) and that the platform switch ships off.

link-carriers.reason: KK then XX on HTTPS polling (transport.go) and MQTT (transport_mqtt.go), through the shared noiseChannel in transport_noise.go: a KK answer that does not authenticate, or over HTTPS a request answered 401 or 403 during the exchange, is followed at once by one XX attempt in the same connect, whose outcome is the connect's. runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.
